Editing switches to a custom strategy. --ip and --port are set by the app. Positions accept zapret markers (host, endhost, sld, midsld, endsld, sniext, method, e.g. midsld+1); -M accepts tpws modifications (hostcase, hostdot, hosttab, hostnospace, hostpad=N, methodspace, methodeol, unixeol).

Try strategies one by one against chosen sites, like zapret\'s blockcheck

Each strategy is started as a local proxy and the sites are opened over HTTPS through it: connection, TLS handshake with certificate check, HTTP response and up to 128 KB of the body. Works with the VPN on or off. QUIC and calls (UDP) are checked in the UDP mode.

HTTP: split after the method, hostcase and hostdot; TLS: split in the middle of the second-level domain and a TLS record at the SNI extension
Create, import and edit lists of domains (zapret format)
One domain per line, subdomains included, # starts a comment. Use a list in the "Where to apply" setting or in arguments as {list:name}, e.g. --hosts {list:youtube}.
A list with this name exists

Accepted: domains, URLs, *.example.com, several per line. Gzip files can be imported.

The engine notes domains where it still sees a block (reset, timeout, redirect, TLS error), as zapret autohostlist does. A blocked connection is tried once more with the first group of the strategy, and a 4 s timeout is added if the strategy has none.
Domains that failed with the current strategy
Domains where a block was detected even with the strategy applied. Add them to a list, e.g. to try another strategy only for them.
Recording is off. Turn on \"Record blocked domains\" in Settings → Debugging and reconnect.

Any HTTP answer, even 404 or 403, means the connection got through DPI: the status is what the server itself replied. A block shows up as a reset, a timeout, a stalled or truncated response, a wrong certificate or a redirect to a block page.

Each site is checked over QUIC (HTTP/3, UDP 443): a QUIC Initial with the site name is sent and any server reply counts as passed. STUN servers used by calls are checked too: %1$s. Without root, UDP desync means fake datagrams with a low TTL before the real ones.
Checks the device, the engine and the network and makes a report to send to the developer

Runs about 80 checks in two or three minutes: permissions, Private DNS, battery optimization, fake payloads; the engine against local servers on this phone (SOCKS5, TCP with split and disorder, UDP with fakes); every preset; then DNS, HTTPS, QUIC and STUN without bypass and with the current strategy; at the end Discord (site, app gateway, CDN) with a dozen strategies, zapret-termux, --mss 88 and allowed-SNI fakes among them. The report includes the end of the journal. The VPN can stay on.

Every strategy against hundreds or thousands of domains from site groups and host lists; results saved as a matrix

A long run without stages: every strategy of the chosen set opens every domain, as many times as set. A domain counts as opened only if every attempt succeeds. Results are saved as they come (matrix.csv: domain × strategy, a reason code per attempt) and can be shared; the multi-strategy is built from them. Runs in the background with a notification; it can take hours.
Host lists also appear here: download them in Settings → Host lists → Lists from repositories.

Route only one app through the VPN while you use it and save every domain it opens as a host list

Pick an app: the VPN restarts and routes only that app, with the current strategy. Open the app and use the parts that do not work (calls, avatars, videos), then come back and tap Stop. Every host it connected to is listed, hosts where the engine saw a block are marked, and the domains can be saved as a host list for a strategy of their own (deep check, multi-strategy, host scope).
